meta.title: 40 albums · 40 days
about: Music has been the through-line of my whole life. I've been to countless shows, I've played various instruments, and I've spent years collecting records. Turning 40 felt like the right time to look back at some of the albums that got me here.

These aren't my 40 favorite albums. I couldn't pick those if my life depended on it. Plenty of these would make that list, and every one would be in my top 100, but this list is about more than favorites.

Every one of these is tied to a place and a time. I can still remember the first time I heard each of them, or what I was doing when I played them the most. On a crappy Panasonic RX-DS515 boombox on the floor of my bedroom. Driving around in my car at 16, 17, 18 with the windows down. Sleeping on the floor of the bus on the way to a different college town for a lacrosse game. Screen-printing gig posters in the art building at Mizzou. Moving to Chicago, then Denver, then Chicago again, then Denver again.

These albums are special to me in other ways. Some of them introduced me to a genre I didn't know I'd love, or pulled me back into one I'd walked away from years earlier. Some had me digging through the band's back catalog until they became one of my favorite bands. And some just weirdly fit my life at that stage.
Each day you'll find where I was when I first heard it, and why it stuck.

albums.title: Weezer (Green Album)
albums.discovered: Late spring 2001, from a friend's "cool" older brother
blurb: School was out. It was the summer before my freshman year of high school, and I spent every day of it blaring this album. Probably the best summer of my life in terms of music? This is one of many 2001 records on this list.
_Let's get this out of the way: the Blue Album is arguably my favorite Weezer record, but Green is the one that got me into Weezer, and prompted the deep dive back into their earlier albums._

I had a Green Album poster on my childhood bedroom wall. It's one of the only posters I can remember from that room, before I moved into the basement. I can remember studying it up close, dissecting every sticker on Rivers' guitar, and I _still_ want a lightning bolt guitar strap. That summer I got my first pair of Converse All Stars, navy blue low tops. Because that was what people who listened to Weezer wore, right??

I'd crank this album night and day on my Frankensteined speaker system: I cut a bunch of holes in a sheet of plywood, took apart every speaker in the house, and reassembled them in a massive wall built into my bookshelf. I was still early in learning how to play the bass, and I loved that I could play along to all these songs.
This album takes me right back to my childhood bedroom. Blue carpet, red bed frame, green album.

albums.title: Merriweather Post Pavilion
blurb: Is there anything more fitting than Animal Collective and art school?

A few days into January 2009, my buddy Jim texted me that he'd found a leak and it was probably the album of the year. I'll never forget that text. I can't remember if I waited for the official release or not, but I do remember exactly where I was the first time I heard it: the screen-printing lab in the Mizzou art building.
It became the soundtrack to the spring semester of my senior year, and it dominated my entire 2009.

It feels like the right record to start this countdown with. It was one of my favorites almost from the first listen, barely a week into the year. And it came out right about halfway through my life so far. Right in the middle felt like the best place to start.

albums.title: Third Eye Blind
albums.discovered: Summer 1997, on the radio. Really "heard" it a decade later.
blurb: If you were around in the summer of 1997, this album is permanently burned into your brain. It was everywhere. On the radio, on MTV, in movies. There was no escaping it. I was 10, and like everyone else, I knew every single word to "Semi-Charmed Life" and "How's It Going to Be." And I loved those songs. They were fun, they were loud, and they were slightly edgy for a soon-to-be 5th grader? (I obviously didn't know "Semi-Charmed Life" was about crystal meth...)

And that's kind of where my story with the album ended. Until college, when my roommate Ted went on and on about how amazing the entire tracklist was and how pivotal it was to our youth. When Third Eye Blind came to the Blue Note in Columbia two days after my 23rd birthday, he convinced us all to get tickets. Was it a school night? Yes. But as a super senior, it was my obligation to go. So I loaded the album onto my 160GB iPod Classic and realized I'd never really listened past the singles.

This album has absolutely no skips. The very first track, "Losing a Whole Year," is incredible, and _might_ be one of my favorite songs of all time. I became obsessed all over again, with the songs and with the feeling of summer '97. It's an album I'll play for a week straight, pretty much once a year, every year.

albums.title: Wondrous Bughouse
blurb: I remember NPR putting up the full album stream a week before it came out, and I had it on repeat. I'm pretty sure I went to the record store the day it came out to buy it on vinyl.

It was a big part of why Megan and I decided to go to the Sasquatch! Music Festival in 2013. For a millennial at the tail end of his indie sleaze era, that lineup was the absolute pinnacle of everything I was into at the time: Vampire Weekend, The Postal Service (10th anniversary of _Give Up_ 😭), The xx, Japandroids, Grimes, Toro y Moi, Tame Impala, Arctic Monkeys, Youth Lagoon... seriously, just look at this masterpiece of a [lineup](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5e66d1368e1e4e634cd9eef6/1635627081518-S6ML848556OGKJJZVOOE/festival_sasquatch_poster_yellow.png?format=1500w). And the cherry on top was [Draplin's](https://www.draplin.com/work/festivals/sasquatch) festival identity. The Gorge that spring was like the Super Bowl for graphic designers.

This album takes me back to our first apartment in Denver, my first year really getting into collecting vinyl (it was one of the first records I owned), exploring the mountains of Colorado, and being 26 years old and blissfully unaware of any real concerns in life.

albums.title: Lola Versus Powerman and the Moneygoround, Part One
albums.discovered: A few months before our wedding in 2016.
blurb: One more, because this list wouldn't be complete without it.

I first heard "Strangers" in _The Darjeeling Limited_, and Megan and I picked it for our wedding song in 2016. It isn't a love song. Dave Davies has said it's about getting through the hard stuff together, and a connection between people that's deeper than words. To me there's something spiritual in it. "We are not two, we are one." stuck with both of us, and it felt perfect for our first dance. I even printed it on our wedding invites.

After the wedding I bought a vintage vinyl pressing of the album and started listening to it a lot, and the whole record really grew on me. I can't hear The Kinks now without thinking of our wedding day.
